name: Ethical Purchasing Group - SIA Project 22 23
description:
The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS),
    known in Italian as a Gruppo di Acquisto Solidale (GAS), associated with a
    km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The purpose of the system is to connect
    groups of customers with local farmers and store employees, supporting a
    conscious purchasing process based on knowledge of product origin, quality,
    characteristics, availability, and price.

    The operating cycle of the purchasing group is organized on a weekly basis.
    Farmers provide estimates of the products they can supply between Friday
    at noon and Saturday morning. For each available product, farmers specify
    the product type, quantity, price, and optionally additional crop
    characteristics such as size, quality, or ripeness.

    The information system maintains a catalogue of products containing
    descriptions, photographs, the unit of measurement used for sale, and the
    minimum and maximum quantities that can be ordered. Each availability
    entered by a farmer refers to one of the products contained in the catalogue.

    Customers can browse the offers provided by the different farmers and place
    orders by selecting products and specifying the desired quantities. Customers
    are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of
    people, and only the registered representative of each group can submit an
    order.

    Orders can be entered directly by customers through the web system or by
    store employees on behalf of customers. Before an order can be confirmed,
    the system checks that the quantities selected respect the minimum order
    constraints defined for each product. If the minimum quantities are not met,
    the customer must modify the order. After completion, the system sends an
    order summary to the customer by email.

    Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm
    the actual quantities available by Monday morning. If the available
    quantities are sufficient to satisfy all orders, the orders are confirmed.
    When the available quantity of a product is insufficient, the system applies
    precedence rules based on customer priority and removes unavailable
    quantities from lower-priority orders.

    Orders modified because of limited product availability are placed in a
    modified state and must be reviewed and explicitly accepted by customers.
    If every product in an order becomes unavailable, the order is cancelled.

    After farmers confirm product availability, the system automatically
    performs payment for the quantities actually included in the order.
    Payments are made through a personal virtual wallet associated with each
    customer. Customers can recharge their wallet through the store at any time.

    If a customer's wallet balance is insufficient immediately after order
    placement, the customer receives an email warning, but the order remains
    valid. If the balance is insufficient when the automatic payment is executed,
    the customer receives an SMS and has until Monday evening to recharge the
    wallet. If the required balance is still unavailable at that time, the order
    is cancelled.

    Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time
    slot for collecting their products from the store. Store employees can view
    the pickup schedule at the beginning of their shifts and prepare the packages
    corresponding to customer orders. When a customer arrives, the employee
    confirms the collection of the order.

    If a customer fails to collect the order at the scheduled time, the system
    sends an SMS reminder. If the order has not been collected by Friday, the
    order is marked as forfeited and the customer's fair-play score is updated.

    Farmers deliver their products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store
    employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities. If the goods
    have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS reminder.
    If the goods have still not been delivered by 8 p.m., the related customer
    orders are updated, the missing amount is credited back to the affected
    customers with an additional 20 percent bonus, and the customers are
    informed of the delivery problem.

    The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer. The score represents
    the reliability of the customer with respect to previous orders and is used
    as a precedence criterion when product availability is insufficient.
    The score is computed from the number of completed orders, reminders received,
    forfeited pickups, and modified orders. Customers with higher fair-play scores
    are given precedence over customers with lower scores when limited quantities
    must be allocated among competing orders.

highLevelGoals: Farmers aim to easily provide information regarding the types, quantities, prices, and characteristics of products they can supply for the weekly cycle.
Farmers want to ensure that the store employees confirm the receipt of their delivered products to validate the supply chain.
Customers aim to easily view and explore the available products, their descriptions, characteristics, and prices from various farmers.
Customers want to be able to select desired products, specify quantities, submit orders, and review their order status and details.
Customers aim to maintain and recharge their virtual wallet and ensure that payments for confirmed orders are processed automatically and accurately.
Customers want to reserve a suitable time slot for picking up their products from the store and have their collection confirmed.
Customers aim for a transparent and fair process for allocating products when supply is limited, based on their reliability (fair-play score).
Customers want to receive timely notifications and updates regarding their order status, payment issues, modifications due to availability, or delivery problems.
Store employees aim to assist customers by placing orders on their behalf, ensuring accuracy and adherence to product constraints.
Store employees want to view the pickup schedule, prepare customer orders, and confirm the collection of products by customers.
Store employees aim to confirm the receipt of products delivered by farmers, ensuring that expected quantities match actual deliveries.
Store employees aim to handle customer wallet recharges, address payment insufficiencies, and manage order cancellations or refunds resulting from delivery problems.
Store employees aim to monitor the progress of the weekly purchasing cycle, from farmer availability to customer collection, ensuring smooth operations.
lowLevelGoals: Enable the farmer to view a comprehensive list of all predefined product types (e.g., 'Carrots', 'Apples', 'Milk') available for selection when submitting availability.
Enable the farmer to identify the unique identifier and date range of the current active weekly cycle for which product availability can be submitted.

Allow the farmer to create and submit a new entry detailing the availability of a specific product, including its type ID, quantity, unit price, descriptive characteristics (e.g., 'organic', 'large'), and the target weekly cycle ID.

Allow the farmer to modify the quantity, unit price, or descriptive characteristics of an already submitted product availability entry for a given weekly cycle, identified by its unique availability ID.
Allow the farmer to fetch a list of all product availability entries they have previously submitted for a specified weekly cycle, including all associated details.
The farmer can send a request to the system to retrieve a list of all their deliveries that are currently awaiting confirmation from a store.
The farmer can send a request to the system to retrieve the current confirmation status (e.g., 'pending', 'confirmed', 'rejected') for a specific delivery using its unique identifier.
The farmer can send a request to the system to retrieve a list of all delivery confirmation notifications they have received from store employees.
The farmer can send a request to the system to record the details of a delivery made, including product items and quantities, to initiate the store's confirmation process.
The farmer can send a request to the system to trigger a reminder notification to the responsible store employee for a specific delivery that is pending confirmation beyond its expected timeframe.

The farmer can send a request to the system to retrieve comprehensive details of a specific delivery that has been confirmed, including the confirming employee's ID, confirmation timestamp, and any associated notes.
The farmer can send a request to the system to retrieve comprehensive details of a specific delivery that has been rejected, including the reason for rejection and any associated notes.
The farmer can send a request to the system to retrieve a chronological record of all their past deliveries, showing their final confirmation status (confirmed, rejected, or forfeited).
The system shall allow customers to request and receive a paginated list of all currently available product offers, including basic information like product name, farmer, and a summary price.

The system shall allow customers to request and receive comprehensive details for a selected product offer, including its full description, specific characteristics (e.g., weight, origin), and exact pricing.
The system shall allow customers to apply a filter to the list of product offers based on predefined product categories (e.g., 'Vegetables', 'Fruits', 'Dairy'), returning only matching offers.
The system shall allow customers to apply a filter to the list of product offers to view only those provided by a specific farmer, identified by their unique ID.
The system shall allow customers to submit a keyword or phrase to search for relevant product offers, returning a list of offers whose names or descriptions contain the specified keyword.
The system shall allow customers to sort the displayed list of product offers by their price, either in ascending or descending order.
The system shall allow customers to add a selected product offer, specifying quantity, to their temporary shopping cart.
The system shall allow customers to modify the quantity of an item already present in their shopping cart.
The system shall allow customers to remove a specific product item from their shopping cart.
The system shall allow customers to finalize their shopping cart contents into a new pending order.
The system shall allow customers to view a paginated list of their orders, including status and basic details.
The system shall allow customers to request and receive comprehensive details for a selected order, including items, quantities, prices, and current status.
The system shall allow customers to check their available funds in the virtual wallet.
The system shall allow customers to request to add funds to their virtual wallet, specifying the amount.
The system shall allow customers to authorize payment for a pending order using their virtual wallet balance.
The system shall allow customers to view a paginated list of all debit and credit transactions associated with their virtual wallet.
The system shall allow customers to view a list of available time slots for collecting a particular order.
The system shall allow customers to select and confirm a preferred time slot for collecting their order.
The system shall allow customers to cancel an existing pickup slot reservation for an order.
The system shall allow customers to check the real-time status of their order (e.g., 'pending', 'ready for pickup', 'collected') and any associated notifications.
Allow the customer to retrieve a paginated list of all products currently available for purchase.
Enable the customer to retrieve comprehensive details (e.g., description, price, stock level, images) for a specific product using its unique identifier.
Allow the customer to filter and view products offered by a specific farmer.
Permit the customer to add a specified quantity of a particular product to their active shopping cart.
Allow the customer to modify the quantity of an existing product within their active shopping cart.
Enable the customer to remove a specific product entirely from their active shopping cart.
Allow the customer to retrieve a detailed list of all products and their quantities currently in their active shopping cart.
Allow the customer to finalize and submit their shopping cart as a new order, transitioning it from a cart to an entered order state, awaiting farmer confirmation and minimum quantity validation.
Permit the customer to modify quantities or items within an order that is currently in an 'entered' state, before it is confirmed by farmers.
Enable the customer to retrieve a list of all orders they have previously placed, including basic status information.
Permit the customer to retrieve comprehensive details for a specific order, including items, quantities, total cost, collection information, and current status, using its unique order ID.
Allow the customer to initiate a request to cancel a specific order, provided it is within an eligible status for cancellation.
Enable the customer to add funds to their personal virtual wallet, initiating the payment process.
Allow the customer to view their current virtual wallet balance.
Permit the customer to review and explicitly accept system-proposed modifications to an order (e.g., due to product unavailability leading to quantity reduction).
Enable the customer to view the status of their orders, including any system-initiated cancellations (e.g., due to insufficient balance or product unavailability).
Allow the customer to select and reserve an available time slot for collecting a placed order from the store.
Enable the customer to view their current fair-play reliability score.
Allow the customer to view warnings or notifications related to insufficient virtual wallet balance before or during order processing.
Enable the customer to view notifications or reminders regarding uncollected orders.
Allow a store employee to record the successful delivery of products from a farmer to the store's inventory, updating stock levels.
Enable a store employee to update the status of a specific customer order to 'prepared', indicating it is ready for collection.
Allow a store employee to confirm the successful collection of an order by a customer, updating the order status to 'collected'.
Enable a store employee to process and confirm an in-store request to add funds to a customer's virtual wallet, updating their balance.
The customer wants to query the system to get their current virtual wallet balance.
The customer wants to query the system to get a list of all past transactions (deposits, deductions) associated with their virtual wallet.
The customer wants to send a request to the system to add a specified amount of funds to their virtual wallet, indicating an upcoming in-store payment.

The system shall allow the customer to retrieve the current status details for a specific order using its identifier.
The system shall allow the customer to retrieve a list of all their past and current orders, including their respective statuses.
The system shall send an order confirmation notification (e.g., email) to the customer upon successful order placement (status 'entered' or 'confirmed').

The system shall send an email containing a detailed summary of the order to the customer upon successful order placement.

The system shall send an SMS notification to the customer reminding them of an upcoming payment deadline for an order.
The system shall send an SMS notification to the customer if their order has not been collected by the designated pickup deadline.

The system should allow a Store Employee to create a new customer record with provided details if an existing one is not found.
The system should allow a Store Employee to search for available products by name, SKU, or category.

The system should allow a Store Employee to add a specified quantity of a particular product to a customer's order.

The system should allow a Store Employee to submit the finalized order for processing after all details are confirmed.
Allow store employees to fetch a list of all customer orders scheduled for pickup on a specified date.
Enable store employees to retrieve a list of all customer orders currently requiring preparation, distinct from the full daily schedule.
Enable store employees to retrieve comprehensive details for a particular customer pickup order using its unique identifier.
Allow store employees to change the status of a customer pickup order to 'In Preparation' to indicate that the order is being assembled.
Enable store employees to update the status of a customer pickup order to 'Ready for Pickup' once all items are prepared and staged.
Enable store employees to update the status of a customer pickup order to 'Collected' after the customer has successfully received their products.
Allow store employees to generate and provide a digital or physical receipt confirming the successful collection of an order by the customer.
Enable store employees to view a list of customer orders that have been affected by a late or failed farmer delivery, including details of credited amounts.
Allow store employees to retrieve a customer's past order history to assist with inquiries related to pickup operations.
Enable store employees to view the current status of any customer order (e.g., pending, in preparation, ready for pickup, collected) to provide real-time assistance during pickup operations.
Allow store employees to view a customer's fair-play score to understand order prioritization or explain related policies during customer interactions.
The system shall allow a Store Employee to query and retrieve a list of all pending farmer deliveries for a specific period or farmer.
The system shall allow a Store Employee to select a pending delivery and view its detailed information, including expected products and quantities.
The system shall allow a Store Employee to enter the actual quantity received for each product item within a specific farmer delivery.
The system shall allow a Store Employee to mark a farmer delivery as 'confirmed' after all actual quantities have been entered and verified.
The system shall allow a Store Employee to log a discrepancy (e.g., damaged goods, quantity mismatch) for a specific product item within a delivery, including a reason.
Store Employee initiates a recharge for a specified customer's wallet with a given amount.
Store Employee confirms a pending wallet recharge transaction after verifying the payment.
Store Employee retrieves the current balance of a specified customer's wallet.
Store Employee queries the system to list orders that currently have a pending or insufficient payment status.
Store Employee processes an additional payment for a specific order to cover any remaining balance.
Store Employee manually updates the payment status of a specific order after resolving an insufficiency (e.g., from 'pending' to 'paid').
Store Employee retrieves all detailed information for a specific order using its unique identifier.
Store Employee initiates the cancellation process for a specific order, marking it for review or immediate cancellation.
Store Employee initiates the process for a full refund for a specified cancelled order, triggering the system to return the entire payment amount to the customer.
Store Employee initiates the process for a partial refund for a specified order, indicating the specific amount to be returned to the customer.
Store Employee records the specific reason or justification for an order cancellation or refund.
Store Employee queries the system to list customer orders that have not been collected past their scheduled pickup time.
Store Employee confirms that an uncollected order meets the criteria for an automatic late pickup bonus to be applied to the customer's wallet.
The system should allow store employees to fetch a list of all farmers participating in the current week's cycle, along with their general availability status.
The system should enable store employees to select a farmer from the availability list and view the specific products they are offering for the current week.
The system should provide a comprehensive list of all customer orders placed for the current weekly purchasing cycle.
The system should allow store employees to select an individual customer order and view its complete details, including items, quantities, customer information, and current status.
The system should allow store employees to create a new order on behalf of a customer, specifying products, quantities, and customer details.
The system should allow store employees to update details of an existing customer order, such as adding/removing items or changing quantities, on behalf of a customer.
The system should enable store employees to view the total quantities of each product ordered from a particular farmer for the current week, consolidating all customer orders.
The system should display the confirmation status for each aggregated order placed with farmers, indicating whether the farmer has acknowledged and committed to fulfilling the order.
The system should allow store employees to record the actual quantities of products received from a specific farmer against their aggregated order, confirming delivery.

The system should allow store employees to generate a detailed list of items and quantities for each customer order, based on confirmed deliveries, to facilitate efficient package assembly for pickup.
The system should provide a filtered list of customer orders scheduled for pickup on a specific day or shift, including customer names and order identifiers, to prepare for collections.
The system should enable store employees to update the status of a customer order to 'collected' once the customer has picked up their items.

[Farmers -> Efficiently communicate product availability] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and fail to represent the entire software system. The description details a complex workflow involving Customers, Store Employees, and Farmers, but the actors list only includes Farmers, and the high-level/low-level goals only cover the initial step of farmers submitting availability. Critical functional aspects are missing, including: 1) Customer actions (browsing offers, placing orders, managing wallets, reserving pickup slots, accepting modified orders); 2) Store Employee actions (entering orders on behalf of customers, confirming deliveries, preparing packages, confirming collections); 3) System logic for order confirmation, precedence rules based on fair-play scores, automatic payment processing, and handling of insufficient balances or undelivered goods (cancellation, refunds, SMS reminders). The current output covers less than 10% of the system's functionality.

[Farmers -> Ensure timely delivery confirmation] The provided actors and goals are severely incomplete and do not represent the software system described. The description details a complex system involving Customers, Store Employees, and Farmers with numerous interactions (ordering, payment, pickup, delivery, fair-play scoring). However, the input only lists 'Farmers' as an actor and focuses exclusively on delivery confirmation. Critical actors (Customers, Store Employees) and their associated high-level and low-level goals (e.g., browsing offers, placing orders, managing wallets, confirming pickups, receiving notifications) are entirely missing. Furthermore, the low-level goals for Farmers include actions not explicitly supported by the description (e.g., 'Request overdue confirmation reminder' is a system-triggered SMS, not a farmer action; 'Retrieve detailed rejected delivery information' implies a rejection workflow not described). The current output covers less than 10% of the system's functionality.

[Customers -> Access and browse product offers] Major omission. The provided low-level goals only cover browsing, ordering, wallet management, and pickup scheduling. They completely fail to address the critical workflow steps described in the software description where customers must interact with the system: 1) Reviewing and explicitly accepting modified orders (when product availability is insufficient), 2) Recharging the wallet via SMS/email prompts when balance is insufficient at payment time (the current goal implies a generic recharge, but misses the specific reactive flow), and 3) Viewing their fair-play score (which is a key metric for customers to understand their precedence). Additionally, the high-level goals provided in the input seem to be a subset (only 'Access and browse' is explicitly listed in the `goals` array, though others are referenced in the low-level associations), but the primary critique is the missing functional goals for order modification acceptance and fair-play visibility.

[Customers -> Place and manage product orders] The provided low-level goals contain significant errors and omissions. 
1. **Contradiction/Scope Error**: The list includes goals for "Store employees" (e.g., `ConfirmProductDeliveryToStore`, `MarkOrderAsPrepared`, `ConfirmOrderCollection`, `ProcessInStoreWalletRecharge`) which are not part of the defined actor set (only "Customers" is listed as an actor in the input). Furthermore, the prompt asks to critique the work on defining low-level *end users* goals, implying the focus should be on the Customer actor. Including goals for a different actor not defined in the actor list is a structural error.
2. **Major Omissions**: The high-level goal "Place and manage product orders" is the only one provided, but the system description involves complex workflows that are not fully captured by the existing low-level goals, specifically:
   - **Order Modification Logic**: While `ModifyEnteredOrder` exists, the system description specifies that if quantities are insufficient, the system applies precedence rules and modifies orders, which then require explicit acceptance. The goal `ReviewAndAcceptModifiedOrder` covers the acceptance, but there is no goal for the customer to *view* the specific proposed modifications before accepting (distinct from just viewing order details).
   - **Payment Failure Handling**: The description states that if the balance is insufficient at payment execution, the customer receives an SMS and has until Monday evening to recharge. The goal `AddFundsToVirtualWallet` exists, but there is no specific goal for the customer to *acknowledge* or *respond* to the payment failure notification in a way that distinguishes it from a general balance warning, although `ViewInsufficientBalanceWarning` might partially cover this. However, the critical missing piece is the **collection process** from the customer's perspective. The customer must *arrive* and *collect*. While `ReserveCollectionTimeSlot` exists, there is no goal for the customer to *confirm* their arrival or the completion of the collection from their side (though the employee confirms it, the customer's action of picking up is the physical counterpart, but in software terms, the customer might need to mark it as collected or simply the system updates it upon employee confirmation). More importantly, the **Fair Play Score** is mentioned as a precedence criterion. The goal `RetrieveFairPlayScore` exists, which is good.
   - **Missing Actor Goals**: Since the input only defines "Customers" as the actor, the low-level goals should strictly correspond to Customer actions. The inclusion of Store Employee goals is a direct contradiction to the provided actor list.
3. **Incomplete Coverage of Customer Actions**: 
   - The customer needs to **browse offers** (covered by `RetrieveAvailableProducts`, `BrowseProductsByFarmer`).
   - The customer needs to **place orders** (covered by cart actions and `SubmitOrder`).
   - The customer needs to **manage payments** (covered by `AddFundsToVirtualWallet`, `RetrieveWalletBalance`).
   - The customer needs to **collect products** (covered by `ReserveCollectionTimeSlot`).
   - The customer needs to **review status** (covered by `RetrieveCustomerOrders`, `RetrieveSpecificOrderDetails`).
   - The customer needs to **handle modifications** (covered by `ReviewAndAcceptModifiedOrder`).
   
   The primary issue is the inclusion of non-customer goals. If the task is to define goals for the *defined* actors (Customers), the store employee goals are invalid. If the task implies defining goals for *all* actors in the system, the actor list is incomplete. Given the instruction "Assuming the work done on actors... is ok", we must assume "Customers" is the only actor to consider. Therefore, the presence of Store Employee goals is a major error.

1. **Major Omissions**: The system description details a complex workflow involving farmers (providing estimates, confirming availability), customers (browsing, ordering, managing wallets, reserving slots, collecting goods), and store employees (confirming deliveries, preparing packages, handling forfeitures). The description states: "Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time slot". While employees might assist, the primary actor for this specific action in the context of the description is the customer, or it happens post-payment, not necessarily during the initial order entry phase described in the high-level goal.
   - The high-level goal "Facilitate customer order placement" is too narrow to cover the entire system scope, but since the prompt assumes high-level goals are "ok", the low-level goals must still reflect the full system functionality if they are meant to be representative. The provided actors and goals only cover a small fraction of the system's functionality (specifically, the pickup phase for store employees). The software description explicitly involves Farmers (entering availability, confirming quantities, delivering goods) and Customers (browsing, ordering, managing wallets, reserving slots, accepting modifications). The current low-level goals are a tiny fraction of the system's functionality and do not represent the complete system described.

[Store Employees -> Manage payment and order issues] The provided low-level goals are severely incomplete and contain significant errors. 
1. **Major Omissions**: The system description details a complex workflow involving Farmers (entering availability, confirming quantities), Customers (browsing, ordering, reserving slots, collecting), and Store Employees (confirming deliveries, preparing packages, confirming collections). The current list only covers a narrow subset of Store Employee actions related to payments and refunds. It completely ignores:
   - Store Employees confirming receipt of farmer deliveries (a critical step triggering the 4pm/8pm logic).
   - Store Employees preparing packages and confirming customer collections.
   - Store Employees entering orders on behalf of customers.
   - The logic for handling the 20% bonus for late deliveries is described as an automatic system action in the text ("the missing amount is credited back... with an additional 20 percent bonus"), yet the low-level goal `ConfirmUncollectedOrderForBonusEligibility` incorrectly assigns this to a Store Employee action for *uncollected* orders, whereas the text specifies this bonus applies to *undelivered* goods by farmers.
2. **Contradictions/Errors**: The goal `ConfirmUncollectedOrderForBonusEligibility` contradicts the description. The description states that if goods are not delivered by 8 p.m., the system automatically credits the customer with a bonus. It does not state that Store Employees confirm eligibility for a bonus on uncollected orders. Uncollected orders result in a forfeited status and fair-play score update, not a bonus.
3. **Scope**: The prompt asks to critique the work on defining low-level end-user goals. The current set is too narrow and misaligned with the actual system logic regarding delivery failures vs. collection failures.

[Store Employees -> Oversee the weekly purchasing cycle] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and contain a significant omission regarding the system's operational logic. While the goals cover viewing availability, managing orders, and confirming deliveries, they completely miss the critical action of **viewing the pickup schedule at the beginning of shifts** to prepare packages, which is explicitly mentioned in the description ("Store employees can view the pickup schedule at the beginning of their shifts and prepare the packages"). More importantly, the description states that if goods have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS, and if not by 8 p.m., orders are updated and customers credited. While some of this might be automated, the store employee likely needs to **trigger or verify the delivery status** or **handle the exception** (e.g., confirming the non-arrival to trigger the credit process) if the system doesn't do it purely automatically based on time alone without human input. However, the most glaring omission is the lack of a goal for **viewing the fair-play scores** or **managing customer reliability data**, which is a core part of the system's logic for precedence. Additionally, the goal "Retrieve daily customer pickup schedule" is present, but the description emphasizes preparing packages *based on confirmed deliveries*. The current list lacks a goal for **handling the specific Tuesday evening delivery deadline exceptions** (e.g., marking a delivery as failed/late to trigger the 20% bonus credit), which is a distinct operational task for the employee if the system doesn't fully automate the credit without confirmation. Most critically, the description mentions employees "assist customers" and "handle product collection". The goal "Mark a customer order as collected" is present. However, the description says "If a customer fails to collect... system sends SMS". This is automated. But the employee must **view the list of uncollected orders** or **manage the forfeited status** if the system doesn't auto-forfeit. The description says "order is marked as forfeited", implying automation, but usually, an employee might need to verify. The biggest issue is the **omission of the goal to view/manage the fair-play score** or at least be aware of it, as it's a key system feature. Also, the goal "Retrieve aggregated order summary for a specific farmer" is good, but there is no goal for **viewing the status of the automatic payment** or **handling payment failures** (e.g., if a customer doesn't recharge by Monday evening, the order is cancelled; does the employee need to view this list of cancelled orders due to payment failure?). The current goals are too focused on the happy path of order creation and delivery confirmation, missing the exception handling and monitoring aspects specific to the store employee's role in the "conscious purchasing" and "fair-play" context.

high_level_goal.name: Ensure timely delivery confirmation
high_level_goal.description: Farmers want to ensure that the store employees confirm the receipt of their delivered products to validate the supply chain.

actor.name: Farmers
actor.description: Individuals who supply products and provide availability information.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) are all directly relevant to the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Ensure timely delivery confirmation'. 

1. **Relevance**: All LLGs pertain to the delivery confirmation workflow for the actor 'Farmers'. 
   - llg_001, llg_002, llg_006, llg_007, llg_008 are read/query operations to check status, which is essential for a farmer to 'ensure' confirmation has happened.
   - llg_003 retrieves notifications, which is a valid way to be informed of confirmation.
   - llg_004 'Submit delivery manifest' is the prerequisite action that initiates the confirmation process. Without submitting the delivery, there is nothing to confirm. It is logically part of the 'ensure timely delivery confirmation' cycle as it starts the clock for the store to confirm.
   - llg_005 'Request overdue confirmation reminder' directly supports the 'timely' aspect of the HLG by allowing the farmer to nudge the store if confirmation is delayed.

2. **Duplication/Contradiction**: There are no clear duplications. llg_001 (list pending) and llg_008 (history) serve different purposes (current vs. past). llg_002 (specific status) and llg_006/007 (detailed info) are granular but distinct (status check vs. detailed audit trail). None contradict the documentation.

3. **Missing Capabilities**: The documentation states: 'If the goods have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS reminder.' This is an automatic system action, not a farmer action. The farmer's role is to deliver and then wait for confirmation. The LLGs cover the farmer's ability to track this process. There is no explicit requirement for the farmer to *cancel* a delivery or *modify* it after submission in the context of the confirmation phase described (modifications happen earlier in the order phase). The current set covers the farmer's interaction with the confirmation state adequately.

Therefore, all LLGs are supported and relevant.

high_level_goal.description: Customers aim to maintain and recharge their virtual wallet and ensure that payments for confirmed orders are processed automatically and accurately.

actor.name: Customers
actor.description: Representatives of purchasing groups who browse offers, place orders, manage payments, and collect products.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) align well with the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Securely manage payments for orders' and the actor 'Customers'. 

1. **llg_001 (Retrieve balance)**: Essential for customers to monitor their wallet status before placing orders or recharging. Supported by the requirement that customers can recharge and the system checks balance.
2. **llg_002 (Retrieve history)**: Supports the 'maintain' aspect of the HLG by allowing customers to audit their wallet activity. While not explicitly detailed in the project description as a specific feature, it is a standard and reasonable capability for a wallet management system and does not contradict the documentation.
3. **llg_003 (Initiate recharge)**: Directly supported by the statement 'Customers can recharge their wallet through the store at any time.' The LLG frames this as a request indicating upcoming in-store payment, which is a valid interpretation of the workflow.
4. **llg_004 (Query recharge status)**: Logical extension of llg_003. If recharging is an asynchronous process (in-store payment -> system update), checking status is a necessary capability for the customer to ensure the wallet is updated.
5. **llg_005 (Retrieve successful payment notifications)**: Supported by the system's behavior of processing payments automatically. Customers need to know when payments are successful to confirm their order status.
6. **llg_006 (Retrieve failed payment notifications)**: Supported by the scenario where 'balance is insufficient... customer receives an SMS'. While the primary notification is SMS, having a system query for failed payment status is a reasonable low-level goal for the customer to verify the state of their order/payment, especially since the order might be cancelled if not resolved. It is not contradictory.

No LLGs are clearly duplicated, contradictory, or unrelated. No essential capabilities are missing that would require deferring the branch. The goals are fine-grained but valid.

branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Farmers to Manage Product Availability for Weekly Cycles
branch_001.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete process for a farmer to manage their product availability. This includes viewing available product types, identifying the current submission period (weekly cycle), submitting new availability entries, and subsequently modifying or reviewing previously submitted entries. All operations are centered on the farmer's ability to control and communicate what products they can supply for specific weekly cycles.

branch_002.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the functionalities required for a farmer to oversee and interact with the system regarding the entire lifecycle of their deliveries, from recording them to tracking their confirmation status, receiving notifications, and reviewing final outcomes. They enable the farmer to ensure deliveries are properly acknowledged and accounted for by stores, covering initiation, monitoring, and post-confirmation review.

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Customers to Discover and View Product Offers
branch_003.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe various functionalities that empower customers to find product offers (browsing, searching, filtering), organize them (sorting), and then examine their details. They all contribute to the customer's ability to locate and understand available products within the system.

branch_004.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Customer's End-to-End Shopping and Order Fulfillment Process
branch_004.rationale: These low-level goals collectively define the entire lifecycle of a customer's interaction with the system, from initial product discovery and selection (browsing, cart management), through the order placement and payment stages, to the subsequent management of the order (modifications, cancellations, tracking, collection scheduling), and finally, the internal store operations necessary to fulfill these orders (inventory updates, order preparation, collection confirmation). They ensure a complete and supported customer journey from product interest to order completion.

branch_005.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the essential functionalities a customer needs to interact with and manage their virtual wallet. This includes checking its current state (balance, transaction history), initiating actions (adding funds), and monitoring the status and outcomes of financial operations (recharge requests, fund deductions for orders). All operations are centered around the customer's ability to control and be informed about their virtual wallet.

branch_006.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete process for a customer to identify orders ready for collection, find and reserve a suitable pickup time slot, and confirm the details of their reservation. They all contribute to the overarching objective of enabling customers to successfully arrange the collection of their orders from the store.

branch_007.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide customers with transparency into the limited product allocation process, including the factors influencing decisions (fair-play score, rules), the outcome of their orders, and the ability to make informed decisions regarding system-modified orders due to scarcity. They ensure customers are well-informed and have agency in the allocation process.

branch_008.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Ensure Customers are Fully Informed About Their Orders and Related Financial Status
branch_008.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide customers with comprehensive and timely information regarding their orders throughout their lifecycle, from placement and status changes to collection and potential issues. Additionally, they cover critical financial aspects such as payment issues, wallet balance, and payment deadlines. This includes both customer-initiated information retrieval and system-initiated proactive notifications, all contributing to keeping the customer fully aware of their order and financial standing.

branch_009.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive process for a Store Employee to assist a customer in placing an order. All operations are centered around the creation and management of a customer's order by a store employee.

branch_010.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive set of functionalities required by store employees to effectively oversee, execute, and support all stages of customer order pickups. This includes retrieving order information, managing order statuses from preparation to collection, handling exceptions like delivery issues, generating receipts, and assisting customers with inquiries and policy explanations related to their pickup orders.

branch_001.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Efficiently communicate product availability' is supported by the project description, which details farmers providing estimates of products, quantities, prices, and characteristics for the weekly cycle. However, the bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Farmers to Manage Product Availability for Weekly Cycles' is more faithful to the full scope of the low-level goals, which include not just initial submission ('communicate') but also modifying and reviewing previously submitted entries ('manage'). The term 'manage' better captures the iterative nature of the process (submit, modify, review) described in the rationale and supported by the system's workflow where farmers confirm actual quantities by Monday morning. Therefore, the original goal is slightly narrow in scope compared to the reconstructed intention.

replacement_request.rationale: The original goal 'Efficiently communicate product availability' is too narrow, focusing only on the initial submission of data. The project description indicates that the farmer's role in the weekly cycle involves not just submitting estimates (Friday-Saturday) but also confirming actual quantities (Monday) which triggers order modifications or cancellations. Therefore, the scope must be broadened to 'manage' to encompass the full lifecycle of availability entries: submission, modification/confirmation, and the resulting impact on the order state. The actor remains Farmers.
replacement_request.generation_project_description: The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS) associated with a km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The operating cycle is weekly. Farmers provide estimates of products they can supply between Friday noon and Saturday morning, specifying product type, quantity, price, and optional characteristics. Each availability entry refers to a product in the system catalogue. Later in the cycle, by Monday morning, farmers confirm the actual quantities available. If available quantities are insufficient to satisfy all orders, the system applies precedence rules based on customer priority (fair-play score) and removes unavailable quantities from lower-priority orders. Orders modified due to limited availability are placed in a modified state and must be reviewed by customers. If every product in an order becomes unavailable, the order is cancelled. The system automatically performs payment for confirmed quantities. Farmers deliver products to the store by Tuesday evening, and store employees confirm receipt. If goods are not delivered by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, related customer orders are updated, and missing amounts are credited back to customers with a bonus.

branch_003.rationale:
The original High-Level Goal 'Access and browse product offers' is directly supported by the project description, which states that 'Customers can browse the offers provided by the different farmers'. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Customers to Discover and View Product Offers' aligns semantically with the original goal, focusing on the discovery and viewing phase before ordering. There is no significant overlap with other Customer HLGs like 'Place and manage product orders' (which focuses on selection and submission) or 'Stay informed about order status' (which focuses on notifications). The scope is appropriate for the browsing/discovery functionality. The current low-level goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Access and browse product offers'. 
1. **Browsing/Listing**: LLG_001 covers retrieving the list of offers.
2. **Detailing**: LLG_002 covers retrieving detailed information (descriptions, characteristics, prices) for a specific offer, which directly addresses the HLG's requirement to view 'descriptions, characteristics, and prices'.
3. **Exploration/Filtering**: LLG_003 (category), LLG_004 (farmer), and LLG_005 (keyword search) provide the necessary mechanisms for customers to 'explore' and locate specific products within the catalogue. 
4. **Organization**: LLG_006 allows sorting by price, aiding in the exploration process.

All capabilities are grounded in the project description, which states customers can 'browse the offers... and place orders by selecting products'. The system maintains a catalogue with descriptions, photos, etc. The LLGs do not duplicate sibling HLGs (e.g., placing orders is a separate HLG). There are no missing essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG that are absent from the current set. The decomposition is complete and consistent.

branch_005.rationale:

The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Farmer Product Quantity Submissions' captures the same functional intention but is slightly narrower, focusing on 'quantity' rather than the broader 'availability information' which includes product type, price, and characteristics as mentioned in the text ('farmers specify the product type, quantity, price, and optionally additional crop characteristics'). The original goal's scope is appropriate and faithful to the actor's intention to communicate supply details to facilitate the purchasing cycle. It does not overlap with other HLGs for Farmers (which focus on delivery confirmation). Therefore, the original goal should be kept. The parent HLG 'Manage product availability information' explicitly requires farmers to communicate both 'estimated' and 'actual' (final confirmed) product availability. The current LLGs cover these two distinct steps: 'SubmitEstimatedProductAvailability' (llg_001) handles the initial estimate, and 'UpdateProductAvailabilityToFinalQuantity' (llg_002) handles the confirmation of final quantities. The documentation supports this workflow: farmers provide estimates between Friday noon and Saturday morning, and confirm actual quantities by Monday morning. The sibling HLGs cover other aspects like delivery confirmation (physical receipt), order placement, and payment, which are correctly excluded from this branch. There are no missing essential capabilities or unsupported LLGs.

replacement_request.generation_project_description: The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS) associated with a km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The operating cycle is weekly. Farmers provide product availability estimates (type, quantity, price, characteristics) between Friday noon and Saturday morning. Customers (group representatives) browse offers and place orders, which are validated against minimum quantity constraints. Orders remain in an 'entered' state until farmers confirm actual availability by Monday morning. If availability is insufficient, precedence rules based on customer fair-play scores are applied to allocate quantities, potentially modifying or cancelling orders. Modified orders require customer acceptance. Upon confirmation, automatic payment is processed via customer virtual wallets; insufficient balances trigger warnings and potential cancellation if not resolved by Monday evening. After payment, customers reserve collection slots. Store employees assist customers with order placement, view pickup schedules, prepare packages, and confirm collection. If customers fail to collect, reminders are sent, and orders may be forfeited, affecting fair-play scores. Farmers deliver products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store employees confirm receipt of delivered quantities. If delivery is late (after 4 PM Tuesday), reminders are sent; if not delivered by 8 PM, orders are updated, customers are refunded with a 20% bonus, and informed. The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer based on reliability metrics (completed orders, reminders, forfeitures, modifications), which influences allocation precedence.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description outlines a weekly purchasing cycle involving farmers, customers, and store employees. The current High-Level Goals (HLGs) comprehensively cover the functional intentions of all identified actors: Farmers (availability management, delivery confirmation), Customers (browsing, ordering, payment/wallet management, collection, fair allocation, notifications), and Store Employees (order facilitation, pickup management, delivery verification, issue handling, cycle oversight). Specific mechanisms like the 'fair-play score' are covered under 'Ensure fair allocation of limited products' and 'Stay informed about order status and changes' (as it affects precedence and notifications). There are no distinct, documented functional intentions for any actor that are absent from the current HLG list.

branch_002.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Farmers to Monitor Product Delivery Confirmation Status
branch_002.rationale: The low-level goals collectively aim to provide farmers with comprehensive capabilities to view, track, and understand the confirmation status and details of their product deliveries. missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description outlines a weekly purchasing cycle involving farmers, customers, and store employees. The current High-Level Goals (HLGs) comprehensively cover the functional intentions of all identified actors: Farmers (availability management, delivery tracking), Customers (browsing, ordering, payment, collection, fair allocation, notifications), and Store Employees (order facilitation, pickup management, delivery verification, issue handling, cycle oversight). Specific workflow steps such as product catalogue maintenance, minimum quantity validation, wallet recharging, and fair-play score calculation are covered as sub-goals or operational details within the existing broad stakeholder intentions (e.g., 'Place and manage product orders', 'Securely manage payments', 'Ensure fair allocation'). There are no distinct, documented functional intentions for any actor that are absent from the current HLG list.

branch_012.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential functions for store employees to oversee the entire lifecycle of a customer order, from supplier delivery confirmation and order status updates to customer pickup and delivery failure handling. Concurrently, they cover all critical financial operations related to customers, including processing payments, issuing refunds, managing digital wallets, and viewing transaction histories. These two sets of operations are intrinsically linked as order fulfillment necessitates corresponding financial management, ensuring a complete and accurate customer service experience.

branch_013.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage the Weekly Cycle of Sourcing Products from Farmers and Fulfilling Customer Orders
branch_013.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe a comprehensive operational workflow for a store. This workflow encompasses understanding farmer availability and product offerings, managing customer orders (creation, viewing, updating), aggregating these orders for farmers, confirming farmer commitments, recording product deliveries from farmers, and finally, preparing and facilitating the pickup of customer orders. All these operations are interconnected and essential for the successful execution of a weekly purchasing cycle, ensuring products are efficiently sourced from farmers and delivered to customers.

branch_002.rationale: The project description explicitly states that 'Store employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities' and that if goods are not delivered, customers are informed. While the text does not explicitly state that farmers *view* this status in a dashboard, the functional intention of the system is to close the loop on the delivery process. The original High-Level Goal 'Enable Farmers to Track Delivery Confirmation Status' is a reasonable and supported functional requirement for the farmer actor to know if their delivery has been accepted, especially given the consequences of non-delivery (refunds/bonuses to customers). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Farmers to Monitor and Track Product Delivery Confirmation Status' is semantically identical to the original but slightly more verbose. The original is concise, correctly scoped to the farmer's need for visibility on the delivery confirmation event, and does not overlap with the 'Manage product availability information' goal (which focuses on the *input* of availability, not the *output* of delivery confirmation). Therefore, the original goal is supported and appropriately scoped. The parent HLG requires farmers to monitor the status of their product deliveries, specifically to confirm if store employees have acknowledged and confirmed receipt. The current LLGs cover: 1) retrieving a list of deliveries with status (llg_001), 2) retrieving specific confirmation status (llg_002), 3) retrieving detailed confirmation info including quantities, timestamp, and employee identity (llg_003), and 4) filtering by status (llg_004). These capabilities collectively provide the necessary visibility into the delivery confirmation process as described in the documentation ('Store employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities'). The decomposition is complete, atomic, and aligned with the parent goal. No essential capabilities are missing, and no LLGs are contradicted by the documentation.

Specifically, 'Verify and confirm farmer deliveries' covers the delivery confirmation aspect, and 'Efficiently manage product pickup operations' covers the customer pickup aspect. Furthermore, the description mentions 'refunds' and 'bonuses', but the project description states that the system automatically handles payments and credits (bonuses) to customers; store employees do not manually process refunds or bonuses, they only confirm deliveries and pickups. The financial management (wallet recharges) is primarily a customer action, though employees might assist, it is not the core 'financial account management' described. The core operational tasks of the employee (delivery confirmation, pickup management, order entry) are already covered by specific, well-scoped HLGs. Therefore, this generic HLG should be removed to avoid redundancy and incorrect scoping of financial responsibilities.

branch_013.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Oversee the weekly purchasing cycle' is too generic and passive ('oversee', 'monitor') compared to the active operational responsibilities of Store Employees described in the project description and supported by the bottom-up reconstruction. The reconstruction 'Manage the Weekly Cycle of Sourcing Products from Farmers and Fulfilling Customer Orders' accurately captures the active management role. Furthermore, the existing HLGs for Store Employees ('Facilitate customer order placement', 'Efficiently manage product pickup operations', 'Verify and confirm farmer deliveries', 'Manage Customer Orders and Financial Accounts') already cover the specific functional aspects of this cycle. Keeping a broad, generic 'Oversee' goal alongside these specific goals creates redundancy and lacks the precision of the reconstructed goal. Therefore, the original goal should be rewritten to align with the more precise and active nature of the reconstructed goal, or potentially removed if the specific goals are deemed sufficient. However, given the instruction to rewrite if the original is 'too generic' or 'less faithful', and the reconstruction provides a better, more comprehensive summary of the employee's primary operational duty that ties the specific tasks together, a rewrite is the most appropriate action to ensure the goal hierarchy is precise and non-redundant in its top-level abstraction.

replacement_request.generation_project_description: The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS) associated with a km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The operating cycle is weekly. Farmers provide product estimates (type, quantity, price, characteristics) between Friday noon and Saturday morning. Customers (group representatives) browse offers and place orders, which are validated against minimum quantity constraints. Orders remain in an 'entered' state until farmers confirm actual availability by Monday morning. If availability is insufficient, precedence rules based on customer fair-play scores are applied to modify or cancel orders. Modified orders require customer acceptance. Upon confirmation, automatic payment is processed via customer virtual wallets; insufficient balances trigger warnings and potential cancellation if not resolved by Monday evening. After payment, customers reserve pickup slots. Store employees view the pickup schedule, prepare packages, and confirm collection. If customers fail to collect, reminders are sent, and orders may be forfeited, affecting the fair-play score. Farmers deliver products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store employees confirm receipt. If delivery is late (after 4 p.m.), reminders are sent; if not delivered by 8 p.m., orders are updated, customers are refunded with a 20% bonus, and informed. The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer, calculated from order history, reminders, forfeitures, and modifications, which serves as the precedence criterion for allocation.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description outlines a weekly purchasing cycle involving farmers, customers, and store employees. The current High-Level Goals (HLGs) comprehensively cover the functional intentions of all identified actors: Farmers (availability management, delivery tracking), Customers (browsing, ordering, payment/wallet management, collection, fair allocation, notifications), and Store Employees (order placement assistance, pickup management, delivery verification, financial oversight, cycle monitoring). Specific workflow steps such as product catalogue maintenance, minimum quantity validation, precedence rule application, and fair-play score calculation are operational details or sub-goals already covered by the broader stakeholder intentions (e.g., 'Place and manage product orders', 'Ensure fair allocation of limited products', 'Manage Customer Orders and Financial Accounts'). No distinct, documented functional intention at the actor level is missing from the current list.

branch_012.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Customer Order Lifecycle and Financial Transactions
branch_012.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the essential functions for store employees to oversee the entire lifecycle of a customer order, from supplier delivery confirmation and order status updates to customer pickup and delivery failure handling. Concurrently, they cover all critical financial operations related to customers, including processing payments, issuing refunds, managing digital wallets, and viewing transaction histories. These two sets of operations are intrinsically linked as order fulfillment necessitates corresponding financial management, ensuring a complete and accurate customer service experience.

branch_013.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage Weekly Product Sourcing and Customer Order Fulfillment
branch_013.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete operational workflow for Store Employees to manage the supply chain from farmers to customers within a recurring weekly cycle. This includes managing farmer estimates, generating purchase orders, tracking deliveries, receiving products, managing customer orders, generating picking lists, and handling customer pickups, all framed by the configuration of weekly cycles.

branch_012.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Customer Orders and Financial Accounts' is too broad and overlaps significantly with other existing High-Level Goals for Store Employees. Specifically, 'Verify and confirm farmer deliveries' covers the delivery confirmation aspect, and 'Efficiently manage product pickup operations' covers the customer pickup aspect. Furthermore, the financial management described (wallet recharges, payments, refunds, bonuses) is largely automated by the system or handled by customers (recharging) and farmers (crediting), with store employees primarily facilitating the physical transaction or viewing schedules. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Customer Order Lifecycle and Financial Transactions' is still too generic and overlaps with the specific operational goals already present. The core unique intention of store employees regarding the *lifecycle* is better captured by the combination of 'Facilitate customer order placement', 'Efficiently manage product pickup operations', and 'Verify and confirm farmer deliveries'. Keeping a separate, broad HLG for 'Managing Orders and Financial Accounts' creates redundancy and ambiguity, as the specific operational tasks are already covered by more precise HLGs. Therefore, this HLG should be removed to avoid semantic overlap and maintain a clean goal hierarchy.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description outlines a weekly cycle involving farmers, customers, and store employees. The current High-Level Goals (HLGs) comprehensively cover the functional intentions of all identified actors: Farmers (availability management, delivery tracking), Customers (browsing, ordering, payment, collection, fair allocation, notifications), and Store Employees (order placement assistance, pickup management, delivery verification, financial/order lifecycle management, and overall cycle coordination). Specific workflow steps such as product catalogue maintenance, minimum quantity validation, wallet recharging, SMS/email notifications, and fair-play score calculation are either explicitly covered by existing broad goals (e.g., 'Securely manage payments', 'Stay informed about order status', 'Ensure fair allocation') or are technical/operational details that do not constitute distinct, missing high-level stakeholder intentions. No new actors are explicitly defined in the text beyond the three already identified.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale:
The project description outlines a comprehensive workflow for an Ethical Purchasing Group system. The current High-Level Goals (HLGs) effectively cover the primary functional intentions of all identified actors (Farmers, Customers, Store Employees). 

1. **Farmers**: 'Manage product availability information' covers the submission of estimates and confirmations. 'Enable Farmers to Track Delivery Confirmation Status' covers the visibility of delivery receipts.
2. **Customers**: 'Access and browse product offers', 'Place and manage product orders', 'Securely manage payments for orders', 'Conveniently collect ordered products', 'Ensure fair allocation of limited products', and 'Stay informed about order status and changes' collectively cover the entire customer lifecycle from browsing to collection, including payment management, notification handling, and the fair-play score mechanism.
3. **Store Employees**: 'Facilitate customer order placement', 'Efficiently manage product pickup operations', and 'Verify and confirm farmer deliveries' cover their roles in order entry, pickup logistics, and delivery verification.

Specific details such as the 'fair-play score' calculation, 'virtual wallet' recharging, 'SMS/email' notifications, and 'precedence rules' are implementation details or sub-goals that fall under the broader stakeholder intentions already defined in the current HLG list. There are no distinct, documented functional intentions for any actor that are absent from the current list.
